vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Renovate already exempts security fixes from the schedule above — the built-in defaults for this object set `schedule: []` and `prCreation: "immediate"`, so they land as soon as they are found rather than waiting for Monday. Do not restate those here; the only additions are a label so they are sortable and `osvVulnerabilityAlerts` above, which sources advisories from osv.dev as well as GitHub's own feed.

packageRules.description: Bump devDependency ranges eagerly: nothing downstream consumes them, so a raised floor costs nobody anything and keeps the lockfile honest about what CI actually ran.
Never narrow what consumers can satisfy. `dependencies` keep their published range until a release falls outside it — this is a library, so a bumped floor is a breaking change for downstreams.
Separate major updates into their own PRs; keep them off the weekly batch.
schedule: before 6am on the first day of the month

packageRules.description: DocumentFormat.OpenXml is the pin this repo exists to centralize: after ts-pptx and ts-xlsx migrate, neither of them pins an Open XML SDK version and this is the only place it is watched. A bump here silently moves BOTH consumers' validation baselines, so it never batches with anything else, never automerges, and is labelled so the fixture-diagnostic delta in its diff gets read before merge. See docs/sdk-pin.md.
prBodyNotes: :warning: This PR moves the validation baseline for every consumer of this package. CI regenerates `fixtures/diagnostics.snapshot.json`; the delta MUST be in this PR's own diff and MUST be read before merging. Do not merge a snapshot change you have not accounted for.

packageRules.description: The rest of the NuGet tree (test-only packages) batches normally.

Pin GitHub Actions to commit SHAs and batch their updates. The release workflow generates build provenance attestations, so which action version ran is part of the supply-chain story, not an implementation detail.
